agentic.gloss: Systems that don't just generate, they decide and act toward a goal.

decis.gloss: An agent choosing what to say, when, how often and on which channel — per person.

bandit.name: Bandits / RL
bandit.gloss: The maths that lets a system learn which choice wins by trying and measuring.

cep.name: CEP
cep.gloss: Customer Engagement Platform — where this messaging actually runs.

geo.name: GEO

govern.name: Governance
govern.gloss: The controls that make automated decisions safe, explainable and legible.

stories.head: Adobe expands AI stack with Google models, custom Disney models, and agentic workflow tools
stories.plain: Adobe is wiring Google and Disney-trained models into its creative and marketing platform alongside new agentic tools that coordinate content and campaign workflows end-to-end. This matters because it signals how the biggest creative stack is shifting from AI-assisted to AI-orchestrated — a purchase and integration decision every enterprise marketer will face soon.

stories.head: When the buyer is not human: how to market to AI shopping agents
stories.plain: Optimove's piece explores what happens when AI agents do the shopping on behalf of consumers — the agent evaluates your catalog, compares offers, and decides, while the human never sees your message. Marketers must rethink relationship and loyalty tactics designed for human attention spans and emotional triggers.

stories.head: Sitecore launches MarketingIQ to link AI brand-discovery insights to content and campaign execution
stories.plain: Sitecore's new MarketingIQ product connects AI-generated brand-visibility data — how a brand appears in AI search answers — directly to content creation and campaign tools. It is one of the first products to close the loop between generative engine optimization signals and actual marketing execution, making it relevant to both GEO strategy and content ops buyers.

stories.head: Keeping AI agents on-brand: Treasure AI CEO warns of 'AI laziness' as bot volumes explode
stories.plain: Kaz Ohta flags a real governance risk: teams that blindly forward AI output without review erode brand voice and trust at scale. With autonomous agents proliferating, this interview frames the emerging discipline of human-AI collaboration as a core marketing competency — not just a tech problem.

stories.head: G2 unifies four software marketplaces into one platform built for answer-engine optimization
stories.plain: G2 is merging G2, Capterra, Software Advice, and GetApp into a single platform that links reviews, listings, ads, and buyer data to help B2B software brands appear prominently in AI-generated answers. It is a significant structural move in the GEO space, directly affecting how MarTech vendors are discovered and evaluated by AI-assisted buyers.

stories.head: ChatGPT's paid traffic is worth far less than Google's
stories.plain: Data shows paid ChatGPT visits generate only 89 cents per session versus $2.45 from paid Google Search. This hard revenue gap challenges the rush to shift budgets toward AI-answer placements and forces marketers to rethink how they value GEO spend versus traditional search advertising.

stories.head: Connecting with shoppers when the buyer is not human
stories.plain: As AI shopping agents increasingly make purchase decisions on behalf of consumers, brands must rethink how they present catalogs, offers, and loyalty programmes. The piece argues that the relationship layer still belongs to the brand, but the transaction layer is fast being intermediated by autonomous agents — a structural shift in CEP strategy.

stories.head: Adobe brings agentic AI to the content supply chain with CX Enterprise Coworker
stories.plain: Adobe's CX Enterprise Coworker is an agentic layer that plugs into its content supply chain, letting AI teammates coordinate creation, approval, and delivery of personalised content at scale. Combined with Google model integrations and custom Disney models noted in the MarTech roundup, this signals major platform vendors embedding agentic decisioning directly into creative workflows.

stories.head: Claritas brings live optimization to acquisition email
stories.plain: Claritas's new product adjusts audiences and subject lines while campaigns are still running, then uses holdout groups and attribution to measure real lift. This is a practical example of bandit-style learning applied to email acquisition — moving beyond static A/B tests toward continuous in-flight learning that affects how email tools are bought and evaluated.

stories.head: G2 unifies four software marketplaces to help brands win AI-answer visibility
stories.plain: G2 is merging G2, Capterra, Software Advice, and GetApp into one platform explicitly to power answer engine optimization and answer engine marketing strategies. For B2B software buyers, this reshapes where review and listing data lives and how AI answer engines surface vendor recommendations — a significant structural shift in how MarTech vendors compete for discovery.

month.skicker: 30-day synthesis · the shape underneath the feed

themes.head: The Agentic Commerce Takeover
body: Within a single news cycle, multiple vendors — ZEPIC, Jungle Scout, Spangle AI, 5.Y, and Adobe — launched products built on the assumption that AI agents, not humans, will increasingly make or mediate purchase decisions. The strategic question is no longer how to personalize for a person but how to make your product data legible to a bot evaluating thousands of options in milliseconds.

Optimove's framing — 'connecting with shoppers when the buyer is not human' — crystallizes the shift. Brands that optimize only for human attention are already behind; the new surface area is agent-readable product intelligence, structured data feeds, and machine-to-machine trust signals that autonomous CRMs & storefronts can act on.
ev: MarTech Series · Spangle AI product intelligence

themes.head: Brand Governance at Agent Scale
body: As autonomous agents proliferate into customer-facing roles, a new operational problem emerges: who is responsible when a bot goes off-brand? Treasure AI's Kaz Ohta puts it starkly — in a world of billions of bots, brand consistency can no longer be enforced by human review; it must be encoded into the agent's architecture from the start.

Thought Industries CEO Irana Wasti reinforces this from the knowledge side, arguing that AI needs a knowledge architecture, not just a knowledge base — structured, governed information layers that give agents confident, on-brand answers rather than hallucinated ones. Together, these signals point to governance infrastructure becoming as critical as creative strategy.

themes.head: AI Traffic's Revenue Quality Gap
body: Two findings landed this month that reframe how marketers should value AI-referred traffic. Visitors arriving via AI assistants drive 83% more revenue per visit than average — but separately, paid traffic from ChatGPT is worth far less than equivalent Google paid traffic in terms of downstream conversion quality. The gap between organic AI referral value and paid AI channel value is a decision-changing insight.

Retailers layering first-party data into social campaigns face a parallel paradox: sharper targeting can inflate CPMs enough to erase the precision premium. Taken together, the month's data signals that marketers urgently need attribution models — MMM combined with post-purchase surveys — that can distinguish high-quality AI-sourced demand from expensive noise.

themes.head: The ROI Accountability Reckoning
body: Validity Research finds that 61% of marketers are facing C-suite pressure to prove AI ROI as AI takes a larger slice of 2027 budgets — a figure that reframes every other story this month. The problem is not adoption; it is justification. AI productivity gains that stay inside the marketing function and never translate to measurable business outcomes are politically unsustainable.

MarTech's parallel pieces on cheap CAC being expensive growth and on not paying for data you cannot use underscore the same logic from the cost side: efficiency metrics without revenue metrics are a liability in budget conversations. Composable martech architectures are gaining ground partly because they let finance teams trace spend to outcome more clearly than monolithic suites do.

themes.head: Measurement Expanding to AI-Native Surfaces
body: Both Zefr and IAS independently expanded brand-safety & media-quality measurement to CapCut and new TikTok ad formats this month — a signal that measurement infrastructure is racing to keep pace with the explosion of AI-generated and short-form ad surfaces. Where measurement does not yet exist, brand budgets cannot safely follow, making these expansions strategically enabling.

Samsung Ads' launch of three new interactive ad formats on Samsung TV Plus points in the same direction: every new AI-powered content surface immediately creates a measurement gap that must be closed before marketers can allocate at scale. The vendors closing those gaps fastest will gate access to the next generation of media spend — giving measurement companies unusual leverage in the ecosystem.

month.takeaway: Across every layer of the stack this month, the decisive pressure is the same: AI is shifting the buyer, the channel, and the accountability standard simultaneously, and marketers who treat these as separate problems will be outpaced by those who redesign strategy, data architecture, and measurement as one integrated response.
